giris.satir: Peace be upon you, gatekeeper. They call me Master Mihali of the Kemah canyon; I have set waterwheels upon the fierce Euphrates and dressed basalt millstones. Your stream runs idle while your wheat goes to waste in hand mortars; if you would build a mill, bakery, and granary, hear my terms.

secenekler.metin: Setting a millwheel is no small feat, Master Mihali; what do you ask from the village chest?
Who are the family in your wagon? What do you stipulate for shelter and apprenticeship?

pazarlik_ucret.satir: To forge the iron axle and frame the flume, I ask sixteen coins from the public treasury—I do not touch your personal purse. In return, I unlock second-tier watermill, bakery, and granary knowledge for your village.

secenekler.metin: Your fee is fair; what of your family and housing?
We pay the sixteen coins from the village chest, Master Mihali; enter and raise the wheel.
Our treasury has no coin to spare for a master miller; go in peace.

pazarlik_ev_aile.satir: With my wife Despina and my young son Nikola, we are three; grant us a household. If your beds are full we can weather a night under an awning, so long as we are not neglected. My son Nikola knows the groove of a millstone; apprentice him to me at the mill and in five nights he will master the craft.

secenekler.metin: Accepted, Master Mihali; enter with your family, and let Nikola train at the mill.
We cannot meet your terms, Master Mihali; seek another village.

kabul_sonuc.satir: May it bring abundance, gatekeeper. Turning water into flour is my work, guarding the flour is yours. Remember only this: I am a master miller; I do not take sentry shifts on the ramparts.

ret_sonuc.satir: As you please. When winter freezes your arms over stone mortars, you will recall Master Mihali of Kemah.
